finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on line 28 quote shell-related terms inside a degradation instruction; SKILL.md does not execute them. The instruction limits scaffolding and directs backend files into the Convex directory.
The backticks on line 29 format the method name `.collect()` in a data-access rule. This is documentation about avoiding unbounded reads, not Ruby or shell execution.
The backticks on line 30 quote verification commands such as `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx convex dev --once` in guidance. No command is executed by the skill file itself.
Line 30 mentions `.env.local` only to warn that anonymous Convex authentication can rebind it. The skill does not read, print, transmit, or modify environment-file contents.
The environment-file reference on line 30 is a deployment caution about preserving a signed-in user's setup. It does not request secrets or perform environment-file access.
Line 30 recommends checking `npx convex whoami` before choosing a deployment verification path. This is project authentication guidance, not reconnaissance of the host system.

content.value_statement: Turn plain-English product requirements into a reactive, type-safe Convex backend design. Get guidance for schemas, functions, authentication, storage, scheduling, real-time features, and agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Translate plain-English product ideas into Convex backend designs.
Recommend Convex schemas, queries, mutations, actions, and indexes.
Advise on authentication, file storage, scheduling, and real-time features.
Apply design guidance for mobile backends and LLM agent workflows.
Check for an existing backend before proposing a Convex translation.
Delegate Convex implementation work to the Convex expert workflow.
limitations: It is focused on Convex and does not independently implement other backend stacks.
It provides design guidance and delegation rather than guaranteed production deployment.
It cannot verify project-specific behavior without access to the project and its tooling.
Deployment checks may require network access, authentication, and a configured Convex project.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Application Backend
use_cases.description: Describe a product idea and receive a Convex architecture covering data models, functions, authentication, and real-time behavior.

use_cases.title: Extend an Existing Convex Project
use_cases.description: Explain a feature request and get guidance that fits existing backend code, indexes, components, and project conventions.

use_cases.title: Design Agent-Powered Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan chat, tool use, and long-running LLM workflows with Convex primitives and the recommended agent component.

prompt_templates.title: Describe a Product Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to build [product]. Users should be able to [core actions]. Design the Convex backend primitives and explain the first implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: My existing Convex app needs [feature]. Review the likely schema, queries, mutations, indexes, and authentication checks before recommending an implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Real-Time Collaboration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Convex architecture for [collaborative workflow]. Cover presence, authorization, consistency, subscriptions, data retention, and scaling constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Convex workflow for an LLM agent that [goal]. Specify data boundaries, tool calls, authentication, retries, scheduling, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: I need a team task app with live updates, user accounts, and file attachments.
output_examples.output: A Convex backend plan with team and task schemas, membership authorization, reactive task queries, file storage references, and mutations for task updates.

output_examples.input: Add document summarization to my existing Convex application.
output_examples.output: An agent workflow outline covering document metadata, authenticated uploads, asynchronous processing, status updates, retry handling, and protected summary access.

best_practices: Describe the product behavior, users, and authorization rules before requesting backend design.
Provide existing schema and project constraints when extending a Convex application.
Run type checks and a verified Convex deployment before declaring backend work complete.
anti_patterns: Do not request a Convex translation without first disclosing an existing SQL or NoSQL backend.
Do not use unbounded table reads when designing data access for growing datasets.
Do not add parallel databases, queues, real-time services, or object stores without a justified requirement.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It designs Convex backends from product requirements and guides implementation across core Convex platform features.

faq.question: Does it support existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It first checks for an existing backend and then recommends changes that fit the current Convex project.

faq.question: Can it design authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include authentication and authorization boundaries in schemas, functions, and feature designs.

faq.question: Can it plan real-time features?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers reactive queries and real-time workflows, including collaborative application requirements.

faq.question: How does it handle LLM features?
faq.answer: It recommends the Convex agent component for chat and LLM workflows instead of designing a custom messages table.

faq.question: Does it deploy my backend?
faq.answer: It can guide verification and deployment checks, but successful deployment requires project access, credentials, network access, and valid configuration.
